CAREER LEVEL
Entry-level
Product Intern / Product Associate / Junior Product Analyst
A Product Associate helps a company plan, develop, improve, and manage digital products such as mobile applications, software platforms, websites, and technology-enabled services.

Product Associates work with product managers, designers, developers, researchers, marketing teams, and customers. Their responsibilities may include analysing user feedback, tracking product metrics, documenting requirements, coordinating releases, and helping teams prioritise improvements.

A degree in Data, Society & Technology can be especially relevant because it combines data literacy, technology awareness, human behaviour, and understanding of how technology affects people and organisations.
The role is suitable for students who enjoy solving problems, understanding users, working with data, and coordinating cross-functional teams.

Career progression
Career progression depends on performance, experience, company structure, and the specific product track.
Year 1
Foundation
Understand technology, people, and problems

items.text: Learn technology fundamentals, digital systems, and data literacy.
Study how technology affects society, privacy, accessibility, and user behaviour.
Build spreadsheet skills using Excel or Google Sheets.
Learn basic statistics, research methods, and critical thinking.
Observe problems with everyday digital products and document possible improvements.
Practise concise writing and presentation skills.

blocks.text: Year 2
Core skills
Learn product management fundamentals

items.text: Understand product lifecycle, product discovery, roadmaps, and prioritisation.
Learn user interviews, surveys, usability testing, and customer journey mapping.
Practise writing product requirements and user stories.
Learn SQL basics and introductory product analytics.
Understand Agile, Scrum, sprint planning, and backlog management.
Explore tools such as Jira, Figma, and product analytics dashboards.

blocks.text: Year 3
Application
Build a product portfolio

items.text: Complete two or three product case studies using real user problems.
Analyse product usage, conversion, retention, and engagement metrics.
Conduct user research and translate findings into feature recommendations.
Participate in hackathons, product competitions, or interdisciplinary projects.
Pursue internships in product management, product operations, business analysis, or product analytics.
Learn how to assess product impact, effort, cost, and risk.

blocks.text: Year 4
If applicable
Prepare for recruitment

items.text: Complete a capstone project involving product discovery or improvement.
Build a portfolio showing the problem, research, decisions, and expected or measured outcomes.
Practise product sense, prioritisation, metrics, and estimation interview questions.
Learn to collaborate with technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Apply for graduate product, product analyst, and product operations roles.
Consider postgraduate study only if it supports your specific career goals.

A. Product Management
Helps determine what to build, why it matters, which users to serve, and how to measure success.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Product strategy, roadmaps, prioritisation, requirements, and stakeholder alignment.

blocks.label: Target roles
blocks.text: Product Associate, Associate Product Manager, Product Management Intern.
B. Product Analytics
Uses data to understand how customers discover, use, and continue using a product.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: SQL, dashboards, funnels, cohorts, experimentation, and product metrics.

blocks.label: Target roles
blocks.text: Product Analyst, Product Insights Analyst, Junior Product Data Analyst.
C. Product Operations
Improves the systems, processes, communication, and reporting that help product teams operate effectively.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Workflow design, release coordination, documentation, metrics, and team processes.

blocks.label: Target roles
blocks.text: Product Operations Associate, Product Coordinator, Product Programme Analyst.
D. User-Centred Product Development
Combines research and product thinking to identify customer needs and improve digital experiences.

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: User research, customer journeys, usability testing, accessibility, and feedback analysis.

blocks.label: Target roles
blocks.text: Product Discovery Associate, UX Research Assistant, Customer Insights Analyst.

rows.text: Problem definition, user needs, value proposition
Helps teams choose what to do first

blocks.text: Product planning and collaboration
Jira and Notion — organise backlogs, requirements, meeting notes, and product documentation.
Analytics and reporting
Excel or Google Sheets, SQL, and Power BI — analyse performance metrics and present findings.
Prototypes and user flows
Figma — review screens, map user journeys, and communicate product concepts.
Product usage analytics
Google Analytics or Mixpanel — explore user journeys, events, funnels, and retention where access is available.
You do not need every tool before applying. Prioritise product reasoning, communication, basic analytics, and a strong portfolio.
Complete at least three projects that show how you identify problems and make product decisions.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Improve a student learning platform

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Product discovery and user experience
Investigate why students struggle to find courses, finish lessons, or track their learning progress.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Problem statement, user research summary, journey map, prioritised features, and product requirements.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Product metrics dashboard

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Product analytics
Use a clearly labelled sample dataset to analyse activation, engagement, conversion, and retention.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Dashboard, metric definitions, analysis, limitations, and recommendations for further investigation.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Improve an e-commerce checkout

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Product strategy and experimentation
Review a checkout journey and identify potential barriers such as confusing steps, unclear delivery costs, or unnecessary form fields.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: User-flow analysis, prioritised hypotheses, prototype or wireframes, proposed experiment, and success metrics.

For every case study, document the problem, evidence, alternatives considered, decision rationale, trade-offs, and success measures. Distinguish clearly between outcomes actually measured and improvements you only propose.

How to become internship-ready

items.text: Build two or three product case studies.
Learn spreadsheet analysis and basic SQL.
Practise product-sense questions and feature-prioritisation exercises.
Learn to explain a problem, recommendation, trade-off, and success metric in a structured way.
Apply to adjacent analyst and product operations roles to broaden your entry points.

blocks.text: Select courses from reputable universities or established training providers. Certifications can demonstrate initiative, but portfolio evidence and practical problem-solving are usually more persuasive.
Further study is optional for many entry-level product roles. Consider it when it fills a specific knowledge gap or supports a desired specialisation.
MBA or master's in management
Useful for business strategy, product leadership, commercial decision-making, and some competitive graduate recruitment routes.
Master's in Business Analytics or Data Analytics
Relevant for product analytics, experimentation, metrics, and data-intensive product decisions.
Master's in Human-Computer Interaction or Interaction Design
Suitable for user-centred product development, usability, accessibility, and product discovery.
Master's in Information Systems or Technology Management
Useful for technology strategy, digital transformation, enterprise products, and coordination between business and technical teams.

blocks.text: Titles and progression differ across companies. Some organisations hire directly into product management; others expect experience in analytics, business analysis, operations, or related roles first.
Product Associates may find opportunities in:

blocks.label: AI product management
blocks.text: Defining use cases, evaluating quality, and balancing usefulness, reliability, privacy, and safety.

blocks.label: Data-driven products
blocks.text: Using analytics and experimentation to improve customer outcomes.

blocks.label: Digital public services
blocks.text: Making government and citizen-facing services easier to access.

blocks.label: Fintech and digital commerce
blocks.text: Improving payment flows, onboarding, trust, and customer retention.

blocks.label: Responsible technology
blocks.text: Addressing accessibility, fairness, transparency, and user privacy.

blocks.label: Product-led growth
blocks.text: Improving user activation, adoption, and long-term engagement.
These are areas worth exploring, not guarantees of job availability.
Use this checklist to track readiness for entry-level product roles.
Product readiness tracker
I can explain the product lifecycle and the responsibilities of a product team.
I can identify a user problem and support it with evidence.
I can write clear product requirements or user stories.
I can analyse basic product metrics using spreadsheets.
I understand basic SQL and how product data is structured.
I can prioritise features and explain the trade-offs.
I have completed at least two product case studies.
I can present recommendations to technical and nontechnical audiences.
I have tailored my CV and applications for product-related roles.
Mark each skill as you develop it. This checklist is a preparation guide, not a hiring guarantee.
By graduation, a strong candidate should be able to:

items.text: Understand how users, technology, data, and society influence product decisions.
Identify and investigate customer problems.
Translate user needs into clear product requirements.
Interpret product metrics and recommend improvements.
Collaborate effectively with designers, developers, researchers, and business teams.
Demonstrate practical product thinking through case studies, internships, or projects.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Build a foundation in product management, Excel, SQL, and user research. Then create a product case study that combines customer needs, data analysis, prioritised recommendations, and measurable success criteria before applying for Product Associate, Product Analyst, or Product Operations roles.
